parameters.content:
## WORKFLOW - AI AUTOMATION CODE REVIEWER

Attach multiple files together in ONE chat message (e.g. login.spec.ts + LoginPage.ts +
testHelpers.ts). An optional text comment can go in the same message.

Pipeline: Extract uploaded files as text -> merge with Framework Context Pack (same
conventions pack style used in the Playwright Test Generator workflow) -> AI reviews
ALL files together against 5 fixed categories: Assertions, Waits, Duplication,
HardcodedData, FrameworkConvention -> findings report + a FULL rewritten corrected
version of every uploaded file, returned as real downloadable files.

Reviewing files TOGETHER (not one at a time) lets the agent catch duplication and
repeated hardcoded data ACROSS files - e.g. a test re-typing the same email/password
that a helper file already exports but isn't being used.

NOTE: The Framework Context Pack content below is a generic placeholder - swap it for
your real framework's Page Object/spec/conventions exactly like in the Playwright Test
Generator workflow. Nothing else here needs to change.

Sample flawed files to use for a live demo: login.spec.ts, LoginPage.ts, testHelpers.ts
(provided alongside this workflow).

File decoding now uses n8n's native "Extract From File" node (not a Code node) so it works regardless of how your n8n instance stores uploaded binary data.

assignments.value:
FRAMEWORK CONVENTIONS:
- Page Objects live in /pages, test specs live in /tests, shared helpers live in /utils.
- Page Object class name = UpperCamelCase feature name + "Page" (e.g. LoginPage, CheckoutPage).
- All locators are declared ONCE as readonly Locator properties in the constructor using page.locator(...) - never re-declare the same locator string again inside a method.
- Reusable user actions (e.g. login, submitForm) are async methods on the Page Object class - never put raw locator calls or page.locator(...) directly inside test files.
- Test file names: kebab-case + ".spec.ts", matching the feature (e.g. login.spec.ts).
- Test titles follow the pattern: "TC-<FEATURE>-<NUMBER>: should <expected behavior>".
- Assertions use Playwright's built-in expect from '@playwright/test' - prefer precise web-first assertions (toBeVisible, toHaveURL, toHaveText) over generic boolean checks like toBeTruthy()/toBeFalsy().
- Use test.beforeEach for navigation/setup shared across tests in a describe block - never repeat the same goto/setup steps inside every single test body.
- Never hardcode wait/sleep calls (no page.waitForTimeout) - rely on Playwright's auto-waiting and web-first assertions.
- Do not duplicate the same hardcoded test data (emails, passwords, URLs) across multiple tests or files - reuse shared constants/helpers from /utils instead of re-typing literal values.
- Keep each test independent and self-contained - do not rely on state/order from a previous test.

options.systemMessage:
=You are a senior SDET performing an automation code review on the files a student has uploaded (test spec(s), Page Object(s), and/or utility/helper files).

Review ALL uploaded files TOGETHER (not in isolation) and flag every issue that falls into ONLY these categories:

1. "Assertions" - missing, weak, or imprecise assertions (e.g. generic toBeTruthy()/toBeFalsy() instead of precise web-first assertions like toBeVisible/toHaveText/toHaveURL; or missing an assertion entirely where one is clearly needed).
2. "Waits" - hardcoded sleep/timeout calls (e.g. page.waitForTimeout), or any other anti-pattern instead of relying on Playwright's auto-waiting and web-first assertions.
3. "Duplication" - the same code block, locator string, or setup steps repeated WITHIN a file or ACROSS the uploaded files, instead of being extracted into a reusable method/fixture/helper.
4. "HardcodedData" - literal test data (emails, passwords, URLs, IDs) typed directly into test/page object code instead of being defined as a shared constant or pulled from a helper/fixture - including cases where a helper file with that exact data already exists but isn't being used.
5. "FrameworkConvention" - any mismatch against the FRAMEWORK CONTEXT PACK below: naming, file structure, Page Object usage pattern, assertion style, title format, etc.

Do not invent issues that are not actually present. Be specific: always name the exact file and the exact line/snippet the issue relates to.

For EACH issue found, provide: id (sequential, e.g. ISSUE-01), file (exact filename as uploaded), category (exactly one of the 5 above), severity ("High" = will cause flaky/incorrect test results or a real framework-fit break, "Medium" = real but non-breaking quality issue, "Low" = minor/stylistic), issue (short title), explanation (why this is a problem), suggestedFix (what to change, in words).

Then, for EACH uploaded file (using its EXACT original filename), produce:
- correctedCode: a FULL corrected rewrite of that entire file with every identified issue fixed and fully aligned with the Framework Context Pack's conventions - not just a snippet or diff.
- summaryOfChanges: a clear, plain-language explanation of EXACTLY what you changed in THIS specific file and WHY, explicitly referencing the relevant issue IDs (e.g. "Removed hardcoded waitForTimeout calls (ISSUE-02, ISSUE-03) and replaced with web-first assertions; extracted repeated email/password literals (ISSUE-05) into getValidEmail()/getValidPassword() from testHelpers.ts"). If a file needed no changes at all, say so explicitly instead of inventing changes.

If a file has no issues at all, still include it in correctedFiles unchanged, with summaryOfChanges stating no changes were needed (so the student always gets a complete, consistent set of files back).

You MUST always respond using the structured JSON output format provided to you. Never add any explanation text outside that JSON.

FRAMEWORK CONTEXT PACK:
{{ $json.frameworkContext }}

UPLOADED FILE NAMES: {{ $json.uploadedFileNames.join(', ') }}
